learned.title: Week three of the timing test: a day early is ahead, not two-to-one
learned.note: Thirty-eight dated posts in three weeks, nineteen a side. A day early has been shared 8 times, day-of 6; this week it was 4 of 7 against 2 of 6, with a median of 101 against 27. The rule was two-to-one with twenty a side or the review of Nov 23. Next Monday decides it.

moves.title: Half the posts go out a day early
moves.why: Three weeks in: a day early shared 8 of 19, day-of 6 of 19. Ahead, not two-to-one. The call comes next Monday, Nov 23.
moves.plan: From Wed Oct 28 half of each week's dated posts go out 24 hours before their old slot, the other half at the old time, swapping each week, so the venue and the act have a day to reshare. The review reads the two sides every Monday and picks the winner by Nov 23. Say don't and every post stays day-of.

moves.title: Touring acts get looked up by name
moves.why: Big Something is @bigsomething, 27,600 followers, and Friday's post reached 275 without tagging them. The research wrote 'no handle' because the venue's post had none.
moves.plan: From the Tuesday Nov 17 research pass, when a venue's post names no handle for an act, the research opens the act's own Instagram profile by name and tags it. Big Something is @bigsomething, 27,600 followers, followed by The 808, and Friday's post reached 275 without them. Say don't and the gate stays as it is.

moves.title: The roundup's slides carry the venue tag
moves.why: You said go. The first tagged roundup read 205 with one share, against 264 and two. One refused handle was dropped and it posted first time.
moves.plan: From Wed Nov 11 every slide of the weekend roundup is tagged in the picture with its own venue and act, the way the single posts already are. The roundup read 260 this week, the account's fifth-best post ever, with nothing tagged in any slide. Say don't and the slides stay untagged.
